title: Lowe's Cuts Full-Year Outlook as Cautious Homeowners Scale Back DIY Spending
excerpt: The home-improvement retailer beat quarterly profit estimates but trimmed annual targets across the board, projecting flat comparable-store sales as budget-conscious consumers defer big-ticket renovations.
body:
• Lowe's beat Q2 profit estimates with adjusted EPS of $4.40 vs. the $4.22 consensus, but revenue of $25.96 billion missed the $26.16 billion forecast.
  • Same-store sales rose just 0.2% in the quarter, well below the 0.8% analysts expected, as discretionary DIY spending remained under pressure.
  • The company cut its full-year outlook to $92 billion in sales and flat comparable-store growth, down from a prior range of flat-to-2% growth.
  • Shares rose roughly 4% despite the guidance cut, as investors credited margin discipline and strength in pro, online, and home services segments.

Profit Beats, Sales Miss

Lowe's delivered second-quarter earnings that beat expectations on the bottom line but fell short on revenue, illustrating the uneven state of consumer spending on home improvement. For the quarter ended July 31, the retailer posted net income of $2.4 billion, or $4.27 per share, flat with a year ago. Adjusted earnings came in at $4.40 per share, topping the FactSet consensus of $4.22.

Revenue grew 8.4% to $25.96 billion, but came in below analyst projections of $26.16 billion. Comparable-store sales increased just 0.2%, missing the 0.8% growth Wall Street had anticipated.

Gross margins of $8.58 billion also edged past estimates of $8.54 billion, helped by the usual spring-season boost and tight expense management.

DIY Pullback Drives Guidance Cut

The bigger story was the revised full-year outlook. Lowe's lowered guidance across nearly every major financial metric, projecting 2026 sales of $92 billion — anchoring the bottom of its former $92 billion to $94 billion range. The company now expects flat comparable-store sales, replacing a previous forecast of flat-to-2% growth.

"Customers continue to be cautious and are prioritizing how they invest in their homes."

— Marvin Ellison, Chairman and CEO, Lowe's

Earnings-per-share guidance was also trimmed to $11.75, from a range of $11.75 to $12.25. Adjusted EPS was guided to $12.25, down from $12.25 to $12.75 previously. Analysts had expected adjusted EPS of $12.43.

The guidance cut reflects persistent weakness in do-it-yourself spending as homeowners defer larger renovation projects. Steep interest rates and sticky inflation have squeezed household budgets, making consumers reluctant to take on debt for discretionary home upgrades.

Pro and Online Channels Offset Weakness

Where Lowe's found traction was in its professional customer business, online sales, and home services — areas the company has targeted as growth drivers under its Total Home strategy. Online sales surged nearly 16% in the quarter, and the pro segment continued to outpace the broader business.

"Sustained growth in Pro, Online and Home Services led to our fifth consecutive quarter of positive comp sales, despite pressure in discretionary DIY spending," Ellison said.

Neil Saunders, managing director of GlobalData, called the results "reasonable" given the tight market. "Lowe's remains a well-run operation, and although comparable growth may come in flat this year, this is not down to any major internal stumbles," he said.

Home Depot Comparison

The report followed rival Home Depot's stronger quarterly results a day earlier, where the larger chain beat expectations and maintained its full-year guidance. Both companies pointed to cautious consumer behavior, but Home Depot's heavier reliance on professional contractors — who tend to be less sensitive to economic cycles — gave it a relative edge.

D.A. Davidson analyst Michael Baker said the guidance cut was unlikely to shift the broader investment thesis for Lowe's, noting the company's earnings power would improve once the housing market recovers.

Shares of Lowe's rose about 4% on Wednesday despite the lowered outlook, as investors focused on the profit beat and operational execution rather than the top-line miss. The stock remains down roughly 11% for the year.
